chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Safwan, from Aban, from Fuzayl, who said:
I said to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him):
[58:22] "Those — He has impressed the faith in their hearts"
"Is it for them, regarding what He has impressed in their hearts, any agency over it?"

key_terms.أُولَئِكَ: Those — the specific believers whom Allah has distinguished by impressing faith into their hearts
key_terms.الْإِيمَانَ: Faith (iman) — the divinely bestowed belief impressed by God into the heart of the believer
key_terms.صُنْعٌ: Agency / doing — any human action, effort, control, or participation in a matter
key_terms.قُلُوبِهِمُ: Their hearts — the divinely designated locus of the impressed faith
key_terms.كَتَبَ: Impressed / inscribed — God's sovereign act of writing or imprinting faith into the hearts

ai.seo_question: Do believers have any personal agency over the faith that Allah has written in their hearts?
ai.summary: This hadith records a question posed by Fuzayl to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) concerning the Quranic verse [58:22], which declares that Allah has impressed faith into the hearts of certain believers. Fuzayl asks whether those believers themselves possess any personal agency or participatory role in that divine inscription of iman. The Imam (peace be upon him) answers with a categorical 'No,' establishing that the bestowal of faith upon the heart is an exclusive act of divine grace and will, entirely independent of human effort or volition.
